title: Direct and Inverse Proportion
seo_title: Year 10 Maths: Direct and Inverse Proportion Worksheets (GCSE)
standard_code: KS4: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
standard_text: Solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion, including graphical and algebraic representations.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE maths worksheets on direct and inverse proportion, y = kx and y = k/x, and proportion problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Direct: both double together (find the value for 1). Inverse: one doubles, the other halves (find the total).
key_sub: For best buys, compare the cost per item, per gram or per litre.
body_html:
How it works

Direct proportion: when one quantity doubles, so does the other (y = kx). Use the unitary method: find the value for 1, then multiply.

Inverse proportion: when one quantity doubles, the other halves (y = k/x). The product stays the same, so find the total first (for example builder-days), then divide.

Example

5 pens cost £3.50. Find the cost of 8 pens.

1 pen costs £3.50 ÷ 5 = 70p.

8 pens cost 8 × 70p.

Answer: £5.60

Example

4 workers take 6 days. How long would 3 workers take?

4 × 6 = 24 worker-days.

24 ÷ 3 = 8.

Answer: 8 days

Common mistakes

  • Treating inverse proportion as direct: more workers means less time, not more.
  • Adding instead of multiplying: if 4 cost £6, then 8 cost £12, not £10.
  • Comparing best buys without using the same amount (find the cost per gram or per item).
  • Forgetting to find k first when using y = kx or y = k/x.

faq.q: What is the difference between direct and inverse proportion?
faq.a: In direct proportion both quantities increase together at the same rate. In inverse proportion, as one increases the other decreases so that their product stays the same.
Find the value of one unit first, then multiply. If 5 pens cost £3.50, one costs 70p, so 8 cost £5.60.

faq.q: How do I solve inverse proportion problems?
faq.a: Multiply to find the fixed total (such as builder-days), then divide by the new number.

faq.q: How do I find the best buy?
faq.a: Work out the price of the same amount for each option, such as the cost per 100 g. The lowest is the best value.
